healthInfo.emergencyNumber: 112 (ambulance), 110 (police), 155 (gendarmerie in rural areas), 112 (also for emergency fire)
healthInfo.healthcareSystem: Universal (General Health Insurance / SGK for residents)
healthInfo.qualityNotes: Healthcare has improved significantly in recent years. Major cities (Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir) have excellent private hospitals with English-speaking staff. Public hospitals are adequate but often overcrowded. Medical tourism is a major industry — especially for hair transplants, cosmetic surgery, and dental work.
healthInfo.pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 9am-7pm. Each area has a rotating on-duty pharmacy (nöbetçi eczane) open 24/7. You can find the nearest 24/7 pharmacy by searching online or asking any pharmacy. Major chains like Grifin and Acibadem are common in cities.
healthInfo.pharmacyTips: Pharmacies (eczane) are widely available. Many common medications are available OTC without prescription — this is one of the easiest countries in Europe for pharmacy access. However, for prescription medications, you'll need a Turkish doctor's prescription.
healthInfo.prescriptionRules: Many medications that require prescriptions elsewhere are available OTC in Turkey. For controlled substances and prescription medications, you'll need a Turkish doctor's prescription. Some medications may require a special import permit.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a controlled substance. A prescription may be required for certain codeine products.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances requiring a Turkish prescription and special authorization from the Ministry of Health.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid pain medications (tramadol, morphine derivatives)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. A special permit from the Turkish Ministry of Health is required.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis / CBD with THC
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis and THC products are illegal in Turkey. This includes CBD products containing any amount of THC.

healthInfo.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Bring sufficient supply in original packaging. For any potentially controlled medications, bring documentation. Declare all medications at customs.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required but strongly recommended.
travelInsurance.tips: Private hospitals in tourist areas often have direct billing agreements with international insurers. Public hospitals are less expensive but may not have English-speaking staff. Medical tourism is well-developed — even for non-tourists, private healthcare is affordable.

recommended: Typhoid (for extended stays or rural travel)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers from most countries.

healthInfo.waterNotes: Do not drink tap water in Turkey. Drink bottled water only. Ice in drinks at reputable restaurants is generally safe (made from purified water).
healthInfo.foodSafetyTips: Turkish cuisine is delicious and generally safe. Street food (döner, simit, kokoreç) is popular and safe from busy, popular vendors. Avoid raw salads in basic establishments — cooked food is safer. Watch out for meat doner kebabs that may have been sitting out. Turkish delight and sweets are generally safe.
healthInfo.medicalTourismNote: Turkey is one of the world's top medical tourism destinations, especially for hair transplants, cosmetic surgery, dental work, and eye surgery. Costs are 50-80% lower than in the US or UK.
